items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the real property law and the state finance law, in relation
to allocating fines to the anti-discrimination in housing fund
items.lawCode: Amd §441-c, RP L; add §80-a, St Fin L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S945

SPONSOR: GAUGHRAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the real property law and the state finance law, in
relation to allocating fines to the anti-discrimination in housing fund

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To establish a special fund to be known as the "anti-discrimination in
housing fund," which will collect revenue from fines imposed pursuant to
section 441-c of the real property law; and to provide funds collected
pursuant to section 441-c of the real property law to the county human
rights commission in the county where a violation under 441c of the real
property law occurred.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends paragraph (a) of subdivision 1 of section 441-c of the
real property law to increase fine limits for violations under this
section from one thousand to two thousand dollars payable to the depart-
ment of state; and further establishes that twenty-five percent of all
moneys received by the department of state shall be payable to the coun-
ty human rights commission in the county where the violation occurred,
and twenty-five percent of all moneys received by the department of
state shall be payable to the antidiscrimination in housing fund estab-
lished pursuant to section 80-a of the state finance law.

Section 2 amends the state finance law by adding a new section 80-a to
establish in the custody of the state comptroller a special fund to be
known as the anti-discrimination in housing fund, which shall consist of
moneys appropriated thereto, funds transferred from any other fund or
sources, and twenty-five percent of all fines and forfeitures collected
pursuant to section 441-c of the real property law.

Section 3 sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

A recent years-long investigation conducted by Newsday, a Long Island-
based newspaper, revealed disturbing evidence of discriminatory prac-
tices on the part of real estate salespersons and brokers. A series of
"testers" revealed disparate and unequal treatment and guidance based on
tester racial characteristics and ethnicity.

Under current law, the department of state has the ability to revoke or
suspend the license of a real estate broker or salesman, or to impose a
fine not exceeding one thousand dollars, for violations under Article
12-A of the real property law. This bill would increase the fine thresh-
old from one thousand dollars to two thousand dollars, and would divert
twenty five percent of the revenues collected from these fines to coun-
ty-level human rights commission offices, as well as twenty five percent
of the revenues towards a new special fund called the anti-discrimina-
tion in housing fund. This new special fund would be established in the
custody of the state comptroller and funds would be made available to
the commissioner of the division of human rights to allocate and expend
solely for grants for duly applying not-for-profit agencies specializing
in anti-housing discrimination.
Counties have earmarked additional resources to county-level human
rights commission offices in the wake of this investigation, and commu-
nity leaders and not-for-profit agencies have been sounding the alarm on
discriminatory practices for years and are playing a vital role in
devising real solutions to this issue; this new fund will help subsidize
the operating costs for these entities so that they can continue doing
the important work they do.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2020: S7852A

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the sixtieth day after it shall have
become law.

SPONSOR: GAUGHRAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the real property law and the state finance law, in
relation to establishing the anti-discrimination in housing fund and
allocating moneys from fines thereto

To establish a special fund to be known as the "anti-discrimination in

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends paragraph (a) of subdivision 1 of section 441-c of the
real property law to increase fine limits for violations under this
section from one thousand to two thousand dollars; and further estab-
lishes that fifty percent of all moneys received by the department of
state shall be payable to the antidiscrimination in housing fund estab-
lished pursuant to section 80-a of the state finance law.

Section 2 amends the state finance law by adding a new section 80-a to
establish in the custody of the state comptroller a special fund to be
known as the anti-discrimination in housing fund, which shall consist of
moneys appropriated thereto, funds transferred from any other fund or
sources, and fifty percent of all fines and forfeitures collected pursu-
ant to section 441-c of the real property law.

Section 3 sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

A recent years-long investigation conducted by Newsday, a Long Island
based newspaper, revealed disturbing evidence of discriminatory prac-
tices on the part of real estate salespersons and brokers. A series of
"testers" revealed disparate and unequal treatment and guidance based on
tester racial characteristics and ethnicity.

Under current law, the department of state has the ability to revoke or
suspend the license of a real estate broker or salesman, or to impose a
fine not exceeding one thousand dollars, for violations under Article
12-A of the real property law. This bill would increase the fine thresh-
old from one thousand dollars to two thousand dollars, and would divert
fifty percent of the revenues collected from these fines to a new
special fund established in the custody of the state comptroller and
funds would be made available to the office of the attorney general for
fair housing testing and to allocate and expend grants for duly applying
county, city, town or village human rights commissions, or other duly
applying county, city, town, village or not-for-profit agencies special-
izing in anti-housing discrimination.

These additional resources will be vital in identifying and devising
real solutions to tackle discriminatory housing practices.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 74 Chapter 687
 
        MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 945-B, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the real property law and the state finance law, in
        relation to establishing the anti-discrimination in housing fund
        and allocating moneys from fines thereto"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill would establish a special fund to support fair housing test-
ing  by  the Office of the Attorney General called the "anti-discrimina-
tion in housing fund," and would provide the rules for receipt of monies
into such fund and the scope of activities for which such monies can  be
made available.
 
  Under  Article  12-A of the real property law, the Department of State
is the licensing agency for real estate brokers and salespersons and has
the authority to sanction a licensee for certain misconduct.  This  bill
would  also increase the maximum fine the Department of State may impose
from one thousand dollars to two thousand dollars and would direct fifty
percent of such fines to the anti-discrimination in housing fund.
 
  I have agreed with the legislature to make several technical and tran-
sparency changes to this legislation that will (i) clarify the rules for
receipt of monies into the anti-discrimination in housing fund  and  the
scope  of activities for which such monies shall be made available; (ii)
authorize the attorney general to contract with entities  authorized  to
conduct  fair  housing  testing;  (iii)  require the Attorney General to
report annually on fair housing testing activities; and (iv)  accelerate
the bill's effective date from sixty to thirty days.
 
  Based  upon  this  agreement  with  the legislature, I am signing this
bill.

  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______
